overall: Saturday in Los Angeles is expected to feature morning patchy fog clearing by around 11am, followed by partly sunny skies and a seasonably mild afternoon. South winds at 5-10 mph with gusts to 20 mph will maintain a marine layer influence, keeping temperatures well below seasonal peaks. Wind advisories are active for the Antelope Valley and surrounding foothills through Saturday night, but coastal and valley areas should see more moderate conditions during daytime hours.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is notably poor. GFS is a significant warm outlier projecting ~84.3°F while NBM skews cool at ~68°F — both well outside the cluster. ECMWF (~76°F), HRRR (~76°F), and WEATHER_COM (~75.5°F) show reasonable agreement in the mid-70s, but the wide inter-model spread (84°F vs 68°F extremes) and prior-day observed high of only 66.2°F signal high uncertainty; both prediction tiers are rated Tier 4 (Poor Signals — AVOID).
max_temp_prediction: The full ensemble (incorporating prior-day obs) projects a TMAX near 75°F, while the NWS official forecast targets only 69°F — a meaningful gap likely reflecting fog persistence and marine influence that purely numerical models may underweight. Probability mass is broadly spread across the 70–79°F range with no dominant bucket (max ~20.8%), pointing to a best estimate around 74°F but with very low confidence. Traders should treat this as a high-uncertainty day given Tier 4 signals, flat bucket probabilities, and the significant NWS-vs-ensemble divergence.
